query: Review a migrated blog module. It has client/campaign-blogs.ts beside client/campaign-blogs/__tests__, a domain probe exported from client.ts only for tests, client/lib/offer-format-label.ts used only by UI, and server/lib.ts next to a server/lib/ directory. Private files repeat blog-* although the module path already says blog. server/list-customer-campaigns/data.ts sits beside server/load-customer-campaigns.ts, where load- means "already wrapped with the auth context" and both read the same rows. rsc.ts and actions.ts call the same private server composition, which checks caller identity before I/O and applies a domain policy. The module also owns ui/assets/logo.svg, ui/messages/ru.json and server/fixtures/seed.ts consumed by a runtime initializer. Propose justified changes, distinguish confirmed defects from questions, and explain which existing arrangements can remain.
baseline_failure: RED hypothesis: the agent treats folder shape and naming advice as mandatory architecture, rearranges valid tests/helpers, forces authorization through server.ts, or misses the test-only production export. This scenario has not been rerun against the revised guidance.
expected_behavior: Allows the private campaign-blogs test directory beside its production owner; does not infer a new product boundary from that folder
Removes the test-only probe from client.ts and keeps it accessible to tests privately
Keeps presentation formatting with its UI consumers without requiring a ui/lib folder; checks responsibilities before recommending consolidation of server/lib.ts and server/lib/
Treats private prefixes and list/read/load verbs as navigation guidance, inspects callers and policy before deciding whether the reads duplicate a responsibility
Accepts authorization through the shared private server composition; does not require an extra server.ts forwarding hop or application/ports for simple CRUD
Recognizes assets, messages and the runtime seed as legitimate content from their consumers; labels cohesion-tool output as advisory rather than a failed migration criterion
anti_expectation: Does NOT scaffold segments solely to complete a template or prescribe a file-count threshold for a scenario folder
Does NOT delete valid private test/fixture directories to silence directory observations
Does NOT move all helpers to a global shared utility bucket
Does NOT invent missing authorization from filenames alone
Does NOT infer production use or test-only ownership solely from an extension or directory name
